title: Sheinbaum Recognizes Victories of Xavier Becerra and Gina Hinojosa in California and Texas
author: El Chamuco Staff
content:
_This article by El Chamuco Staff originally appeared in the[November 4, 2026
edition of El Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/11/04/sheinbaum-reconoce-
triunfos-de-xavier-becerra-y-gina-hinojosa-en-california-y-texas/), a Mexican
political cartoon and news magazine._

**(November 4, 2026).— President Claudia Sheinbaum recognized the victories of
Xavier Becerra and Gina Hinojosa in the gubernatorial elections in California
and Texas, respectively, and highlighted the participation of people of
Mexican origin in US politics.**

During her morning press conference this Wednesday, November 4, the president
said that the results of the midterm elections reflect “a sentiment of the
American people” and noted that both governors-elect have family and cultural
ties to Mexico.

“We are glad that Mexican Americans have won,” Sheinbaum said, referring to
the results of the Tuesday, November 3 elections.

The president highlighted that Becerra and Hinojosa each have at least one
parent born in Mexico and that, in addition to their ties to the states they
will govern and their respective political platforms, they maintain a
relationship with the Mexican community.

> [Post by @El_Chamuco on
> X](https://twitter.com/El_Chamuco/status/2118003713352822895)

> We are very glad that Mexican Americans who are there have this
> participation and this recognition.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

Becerra, the son of Mexican migrants and former Secretary of Health during the
Joe Biden administration, defeated Republican Steve Hilton in California. With
his victory, he will be the first Latino directly elected to govern that
state.

In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott and
became the first Latina elected to lead the state government. Her victory also
returned the governorship to the Democrats, who had not won that office since
1990.

Asked about the meaning of the results and their possible repercussions for
the relationship between Mexico and the United States, Sheinbaum called for
prudence and said it is still necessary to wait.

The president reiterated that her government will seek to maintain a good
relationship with Washington, regardless of the election results, under the
principles of respect for sovereignty, territorial integrity and collaboration
without subordination.

She also noted that trade talks between both countries are continuing and that
it is premature to anticipate whether the new political makeup resulting from
the elections will change the bilateral relationship.
